design.text: Randomized, parallel-group, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial comparing 2 blinded doses of dabigatran etexilate (110 mg bid, 150 mg bid) to open-label adjusted-dose warfarin (target INR 2.0-3.0); a PROBE (Prospective Randomized Open trial with Blinded outcome Evaluation) hybrid design, non-inferiority margin 1.46.

citations.quote: RE-LY is a randomized, parallel group, active-controlled, non-inferiority trial of 2 blinded doses of Dabigatran Etexilate compared with open-label warfarin in patients with non-valvular AF.

This was a Prospective Randomized Open trial with Blinded outcome Evaluation (PROBE) study with 2 doses of Dabigatran Etxilate (110 mg bid, 150 mg bid) compared to adjusted warfarin therapy, INR 2.0-3.0.
The non-inferiority margin of 1.46 for the hazard ratio in the sponsor's study report was derived based on the historical placebo controlled trials using the 95%-95% rule.

population.text: Patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor (previous ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, or TIA; heart failure; age >75 years; or age >65 with diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, or hypertension).

citations.quote: Enrolled subjects had non-valvular AF and at least one additional risk factor: previous ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, or TIA; heart failure; age >75 years; or age >65 with diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, or hypertension.

endpoint.text: Time to first occurrence of stroke (both ischemic and hemorrhagic) or systemic embolism.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint of the study was time to first occurrence of stroke (both ischemic and hemorrhagic) or systemic embolism.

result.text: For stroke/SEE, dabigatran 150 mg bid was non-inferior and superior to warfarin: HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.52, 0.81), p=0.0001 for non-inferiority and p=0.0001 for superiority; 134 vs 202 events. The 110 mg dose: HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.74, 1.10).

indication.text: PRADAXA is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation.

citations.quote: PRADAXA is indicated to reduce the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation.

target_moa.text: Dabigatran etexilate is a small-molecule prodrug of dabigatran, a competitive, reversible, direct thrombin inhibitor; by inhibiting thrombin (which converts fibrinogen to fibrin) it prevents thrombus formation and acts as an anticoagulant.

citations.quote: Dabigatran etexilate is a synthetic small molecule pro-drug for dabigatran, a competitive, reversible, direct thrombin inhibitor, and a representative of a new therapeutic class of direct thrombin inhibitors.

Dabigatran and its acyl glucuronides are competitive, direct thrombin inhibitors. Because thrombin (serine protease) enables the conversion of fibrinogen into fibrin during the coagulation cascade, its inhibition prevents the development of a thrombus.

Dabigatran etexilate is a synthetic small molecule pro-drug for dabigatran, a competitive, reversible, direct thrombin inhibitor, and a representative of a new therapeutic class of direct thrombin inhibitors.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>15%) are gastritis-like symptoms and bleeding. Patients on PRADAXA 150 mg had increased gastrointestinal adverse reactions (35% vs 24% on warfarin). In RE-LY, major bleed rate was 3.3% vs 3.6% warfarin (HR 0.93), any bleed 16.6% vs 18.4%, intracranial hemorrhage 0.3% vs 0.8% (HR 0.41); adverse reactions leading to discontinuation were 21% for PRADAXA 150 mg vs 16% for warfarin.

summary.text: PRADAXA (dabigatran etexilate) was approved via a traditional NDA on the basis of the single pivotal phase 3 trial RE-LY; the Division recommended approval of the 150 mg capsule and the CRDAC voted 9-0 in favor. Approval included a REMS (Medication Guide) due to bleeding risk and two required postmarketing in vitro transporter studies.
